name: Honda S660
hook: Honda's tiny mid-engined S660 was led by a 22-year-old clay modeller with no engineering degree, who beat about 400 other entries to get the job.
story: It's 2010. Honda's car business is turning fifty. To mark it, the company asks everyone, anyone, to pitch a new car. About 400 ideas come in. The winner is Ryo Mukumoto. He is 22. He isn't an engineer. He shapes full-size mock-ups for the designers, and he has been at it for three years. His idea is simple. A small, light, mid-engined sports car you could actually afford. Honda doesn't just thank him. It hands him the whole project. He becomes the youngest project leader the company has ever had, and he gets five years. He picks a young team, most of them under thirty. Six months later, an electric show car that looks almost the same appears in Tokyo. In 2015 the real thing goes on sale. It's a kei car, so it's tiny and capped at 64 horsepower. But the engine sits behind you, the roof comes off, and the man who dreamed it up is still in his twenties.
description: The S660 is a two-seat roadster Honda built for Japan's kei car class from 2015 to 2022. A 658 cc turbocharged three-cylinder sits behind the seats and drives the rear wheels, through a six-speed manual or a seven-speed CVT. The roof panel lifts out. It weighs about 830 kg. The project was led by Ryo Mukumoto, who proposed it in an in-house contest for Honda's fiftieth year of making cars and became the company's youngest ever project leader.
